title: langaccess
description: langaccess audits the language accessibility of a website. Given a URL, the tool renders the site in a headless browser, reads the same address again as the plain server document, and classifies, for each language present, the form of access provided: English-only content, a machine-translation widget, or text authored by the site itself. The difference between the rendered page and the served document is what separates widget output from the organization's own writing, because a translation widget rewrites the DOM and leaves the markup alone. Every classification is returned with the evidence that decided it, the URL and the quoted text, and with the numbered codebook rules that were applied, so a result can be checked without repeating the crawl, and each row carries a read-quality record and the sha256 of the build that produced it. The tool describes and classifies the access a site provides; it does not score how well a site serves any population. Version 0.2.0 names eleven further languages on evidence of the reader's own, refuses non-web schemes and credentialed addresses in auditable_url, separates a domain that does not resolve from a site the crawl could not read, gives a failed read a named cause across a sixteen-name failure vocabulary, and makes the live audit and the re-judge one reader; the agreement figures measured against the 1,992-address gold frame are stated in LIMITATIONS.md.
